summary: Biblios is a quick, elegant filler about bidding on and drafting cards representing manuscripts, scribes, and resources needed to win five separate scoring categories. Its two-phase structure — a card-passing draft followed by blind auctions — makes for tense, fast decisions with a strong push-your-luck feel.
praised: Fast, elegant design that teaches in minutes
Clever two-phase structure combining drafting and bidding
Plays very well at two players and scales cleanly
criticised: Significant luck from the initial card reveal and God's Favor phase
Low strategic depth compared to heavier auction games
Can feel too random for players wanting more control

interaction.kind: drafting and then blind-bidding gold against opponents for the same lots of cards
interaction.detail: Players alternate placing cards into shared lots or their own hand, then bid gold to win entire lots outright, so a move is frequently made to keep a category out of a rival's hands rather than just to help yourself. Virtually the whole game — the lots and the categories being contested — is shared table state, not private tableau building.
interaction.said: praised as a small filler with real bite, built around alternating card draft and blind-bidding auctions where denying a rival a lot is often the point

subsystems: single drafting/bidding engine feeding five competing card categories
scoring.how_you_win: Once the draw pile is used up (bought or discarded), whoever holds the highest total in each of the five categories wins that category's die-value points, and the player with the highest sum across all five categories wins.
